title: Install the Alexa skill
intro: This guide walks you through connecting your Echo speakers to FamilyGest in about twenty minutes. Once installed, just say "Alexa, ask {name}…" to add an event, shopping items, a dish, an absence, a presence or a guest, or to ask who is eating at home, the pending tasks and the planned meals.
alreadyGenerated: An address has already been generated. If you no longer have it, use "Regenerate the address" in the Alexa card, then paste it again into the Amazon console (step 6).
consoleNote: The Amazon console labels may change slightly over time: if in doubt, look for the closest label.

prereq.title: Before you start
prereq.https: FamilyGest must be reachable from the Internet over HTTPS with a valid certificate ({origin}). To check, open this address on a phone using mobile data, Wi-Fi off: the page must show the padlock, with no warning.
prereq.serverUrl: In the Super Administrator console › Global settings, the "Public URL of the application" must be this same https:// address (otherwise, ask the platform administrator).
prereq.account: Use the Amazon account your Echo speakers are registered to: the skill will only work on that account.
prereq.private: The skill stays private (development mode): it is not published, needs no Amazon certification and is free.

prepare.title: Prepare FamilyGest
prepare.name: Choose the invocation name in the Alexa card (currently "{name}"): at least two common words. Avoid made-up names, which speech recognition understands poorly.
prepare.generate: Generate the skill address and copy it straight away: it will never be shown in full again (if you lose it, just regenerate it).
prepare.download: Download the interaction model: you get the familygest-alexa-fr-FR.json file, containing the phrases the skill understands and the family members’ first names.

devAccount.title: Create the Amazon developer account
devAccount.open: Open the Amazon developer site and sign in with the Amazon account of your speakers:
devAccount.profile: On first sign-in, fill in the requested developer profile (free, the required fields are enough).

create.title: Create the skill
create.console: Open the Alexa console, then click "Create Skill":
create.name: "Skill name": the name shown in the Alexa app, for example "Gestion famille". "Primary locale": "French (FR)" (the skill currently speaks French).
create.template: "Template": "Start from Scratch", then "Create Skill". Wait a few seconds.

model.title: Import the interaction model
model.json: In the left menu: "Build › Interaction Model › JSON Editor".
model.drop: Drag the familygest-alexa-fr-FR.json file into the editor (or replace all the text with its content), then click "Save".
model.build: Click "Build skill" and wait for "Build Successful" (one to two minutes).

endpoint.title: Connect the skill to FamilyGest
endpoint.menu: In the left menu: "Build › Endpoint", then choose "HTTPS".
endpoint.agenda: “Alexa, ask {name} what the upcoming events are” (or “… what's in the calendar tomorrow”)
endpoint.summary: “Alexa, ask {name} for today's summary”: events, who is home at each meal and what we are eating
endpoint.url: In "Default Region", paste the skill address copied in step 2.
endpoint.cert: In the list just below, choose "My development endpoint has a certificate from a trusted certificate authority", then "Save".

test.title: Test
test.enable: Open the "Test" tab at the top of the page: set "Skill testing is enabled in" to "Development".
test.type: Type (in French): "demande à {name} d’acheter du lait". Alexa should confirm, and milk should appear on the FamilyGest shopping list.
test.echo: Done: the skill works right away on your Echo speakers (in the Alexa app: More › Skills & Games › Your Skills › Dev).

usage.title: What you can say (in French)
usage.event: "Alexa, demande à {name} d’ajouter dentiste mardi à 15 heures" (add an event)
usage.shopping: "Alexa, demande à {name} d’acheter du lait et des œufs" (shopping) — avoid "à ma liste de courses", often picked up by Amazon’s own shopping list
usage.meal: "Alexa, demande à {name} de mettre des lasagnes au dîner de jeudi" (plan a dish)
usage.absence: "Alexa, demande à {name} : Paul ne sera pas là demain midi" (absence, always with a first name); "… Léa sera là ce soir" for a presence
usage.guest: "Alexa, demande à {name} : Mamie vient dîner samedi" (guest)
usage.who: "Alexa, demande à {name} qui mange à la maison ce soir" (who is home)
usage.tasks: "Alexa, demande à {name} quelles sont les tâches en cours" (pending tasks)
usage.menu: "Alexa, demande à {name} ce qu’on mange cette semaine" (planned meals)
usage.conversation: To chain several requests: "Alexa, ouvre {name}", then your requests one after the other, and "c’est tout" to finish.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.newMember: New family member: download the interaction model again, re-import it (step 5) and run "Build skill" again so their first name is recognised (not needed if the automatic update in step 11 is enabled).
maintenance.rename: New invocation name: save it in the Alexa card, then download and re-import the model (not needed if the automatic update in step 11 is enabled).
maintenance.regenerate: Lost or leaked address: regenerate it in the Alexa card and paste it again in step 6. "Revoke" cuts access immediately.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.amazonList: The request goes to Amazon’s shopping list: the invocation name was not recognised, or the sentence contained "à ma liste de courses". Say "d’acheter…" and check what Alexa heard (Alexa app › Settings › Alexa Privacy › Voice History).
troubleshooting.problem: "There was a problem with the requested skill’s response": check the address pasted in step 6 (has it been regenerated since?). The platform administrator can check the server logs (lines "[Alexa]").
troubleshooting.unreachable: No reaction from FamilyGest: Amazon cannot reach the server. Check the prerequisites (HTTPS access from the Internet, valid certificate).
troubleshooting.firstName: A first name is not understood: check its spelling in FamilyGest, then download and re-import the model.

autoUpdate.title: Automatic update (optional, one time only)
autoUpdate.why: To never re-import the interaction model by hand again, allow FamilyGest to update it itself at Amazon. It also fills in the skill listing in the Alexa app (name, description, example phrases, icon).
autoUpdate.profile: Open the "Login with Amazon" console, then "Create a New Security Profile": name "FamilyGest", any description, and for "Consent Privacy Notice URL" the address {origin}/confidentialite. Save.
autoUpdate.returnUrl: In this profile, "Web Settings" tab › "Edit": paste into "Allowed Return URLs" the return URL shown in the Alexa card (Automatic update section), then "Save".
autoUpdate.credentials: Still in "Web Settings", copy the "Client ID" and the "Client Secret" ("Show Secret" button).
autoUpdate.skillId: In the Alexa console, under your skill name, click "Copy Skill ID".
autoUpdate.connect: In the FamilyGest Alexa card, paste the skill ID, Client ID and Client Secret, then "Save and authorise at Amazon". On the Amazon page, accept: you come back to FamilyGest, which sends the model straight away. "Model up to date at Amazon" appears after one to two minutes.
